claims.claim: Tempranillo 80%, Garnacha 15%, Mazuelo and Graciano the rest, all from the estate's own vineyards.
claims.quote: Tempranillo (80%), Garnacho (15%), Mazuelo y Graciano (el resto)

claims.claim: Graciano is about 3% of the blend (Mazuelo is the small remainder).
claims.note: Single critic figure; the producer gives only 'the rest'.

claims.claim: 13.5% alcohol.
claims.quote: GRADO ALCOHÓLICO: 13,5% Vol.

claims.claim: Total acidity 6.5 g/l. Residual sugar: very dry.
claims.quote: ACIDEZ TOTAL: 6,5 Gr/l. AZÚCAR RESIDUAL: Muy seco.

claims.claim: Five years in barrel, racked by hand twice a year.
claims.quote: Barrica: 5 años, sometido a 2 trasiegas por año, hechas a mano.

claims.claim: The barrels are used American oak.
claims.quote: ages five years in American oak
claims.note: Merchant says used barrels for this vintage; producer page says American oak for the Reserva in general.

claims.claim: Fined with fresh egg whites and bottled unfiltered in 75 cl bottles.
claims.quote: Clarificado con claras de huevos frescos... embotellado sin filtrar

claims.claim: Bottled in November 2017, then rested in bottle in the winery's cellar before release.
claims.note: Two merchants agree on the bottling month. The producer sheet gives no date.

claims.claim: Release date is not stated by any source. Bottling in 2017 and the winery's bottle rest put release in 2018 to 2019 at the earliest, an inference.
claims.note: Reasoning from the Nov 2017 bottling; a Natalie MacLean review from Dec 2020 shows the wine was on sale by then.

claims.claim: 80,000 bottles made.
claims.quote: CANTIDAD ELABORADA: 80.000 botellas.

claims.claim: A merchant quoting a critic gives 75,000 bottles.
claims.note: Conflicts with the producer figure; use the producer's.

claims.claim: The label says Reserva. The estate makes Bosconia Reserva in most years and keeps Gran Reserva for exceptional vintages.
claims.quote: The Reserva is made in most years

claims.claim: Reserva here means at least five years in oak, longer than the minimum Rioja requires for the category.
claims.quote: a minimum of 5 years of ageing in oak barrels
claims.note: The legal Reserva minimum belongs in the shared Rioja place file.

claims.claim: Viña Bosconia comes from the estate's El Bosque vineyard, 15 ha beside the Ebro and about 1 km from the winery.
claims.quote: situated next to the river Ebro... one kilometre away from our winery

claims.claim: El Bosque is 15 ha: 11 Tempranillo, 2 Garnacha, 1 Mazuelo, 1 Graciano.
The soil is a mix of clay and limestone.
claims.quote: The soil is a mixture of clay and limestone

claims.claim: The vineyard sits on south-facing foothills of the Sierra Cantabria, at about 465 m (460 to 487 m).
South-facing exposure gives extra sweetness to the fruit even in a cool year such as 2008.
claims.note: Tim Atkin as relayed by a merchant.

claims.claim: Vines average about 40 years old.
claims.note: Producer page is undated, so the age is not specific to 2008 fruit.

claims.claim: The name Bosconia comes from a Burgundy-style wine the founder made with a lot of Pinot Noir, which he called Rioja Cepa Borgoña. He named wines after French wines.
Producer: intense ruby colour with slight tile (brick) edges, persistent nose full of fruit led by Tempranillo, round, full-bodied, soft, fine and long.
claims.quote: color rubí intenso con ligeros ribetes de teja

claims.claim: Decanter: tobacco, earth and leather on the palate.
claims.quote: tobacco, earth and leather notes emerge on the palate

claims.claim: Tim Atkin: wild strawberry, tobacco and forest floor, savoury.
Suckling: balsamic and high-toned wood, dried cheese and ripe fruit.
Medium body with fine, dusty to polished tannins. More reserved and austere than the 2009, with herbal notes.
claims.quote: beautifully integrated fine tannins

claims.claim: Acidity is fresh (6.5 g/l total) and the wine is dry.
Roasted, strongly flavored meats and game.
claims.quote: carnes tostadas y muy aromatizadas. Caza.

claims.claim: Serve at 18 to 20 C.
claims.quote: De 18º a 20º C

claims.claim: Producer says store it at 14 C and 75 to 80% humidity; it keeps 10 years and more.
Atkin 2020 to 2028; Wine Advocate 2021 to 2028.
Decanter (2021): drink 2021 to 2024.
CellarTracker range: 2020 to 2027.
Rioja 2008 was officially rated Very Good. No serious weather events or spring frost, a wet spring and a wet period after harvest, a mild, drier summer, and ideal weather through the end of ripening.
claims.quote: Año calificado oficialmente como MUY BUENO

claims.claim: The 2008 crop was not large but slightly bigger than 2007, with very healthy fruit and balanced colour, acidity and alcohol.
At the estate, picking ran 6 to 30 October: Gravonia whites first (6th), Tondonia reds from 9th, Cubillas and Bosconia last, finishing 30 October.
Region-wide, harvest returned to traditional dates after warm early years. CVNE picked 1 October to 6 November. Regional crop was slightly below 2007 because of uneven ripening.
claims.note: CVNE is one producer; trade-report wording was seen only in a search summary.

claims.claim: The winery is at Avda. de Vizcaya 3 in Haro, La Rioja Alta.
claims.quote: Avda. de Vizcaya, 3. 26200 Haro (La Rioja)

claims.claim: Rafael López de Heredia y Landeta started the winery in Haro in 1877. He came from Chile with Spanish parents.
claims.quote: came to Haro to start up his business

claims.claim: He was inspired by French wine merchants who came to Rioja after phylloxera hit French vineyards.
claims.note: Producer home page, read through a summary tool.

claims.claim: The winery grew up in Haro's Barrio de la Estación, near the railway.
claims.note: Seen in a search snippet only; the Haro tourism page does not mention the neighbourhood.

claims.claim: The family still owns it. María José, Mercedes and Julio César López de Heredia are the fourth generation.
claims.note: Decanter via search snippet; not confirmed on the producer site.

claims.claim: The estate has about 170 ha, all in Rioja Alta, all owned by the family: Tondonia, Bosconia (El Bosque), Cubillo (Cubillas) and Zaconia (source of Gravonia).
Viña Tondonia was planted in 1913 to 1914 and gave the winery its name. It is the best-known vineyard.
claims.note: Producer says 1913 to 1914; Haro tourism says 1914.

claims.claim: Cubillo (Viña Cubillas) is 24 ha, about 4 km from the winery, with clay and limestone soil. The founder bought it.
Gravonia is the white from Viña Zaconia, picked first each year.
claims.note: Zaconia size (24 ha) is only from search snippets and is left out.

claims.claim: The winery has its own cooperage with three master coopers who build and repair all its barrels.
claims.quote: one of the few bodegas in the world with its own traditionally crafted cooperage

claims.claim: The underground cellar is cut into sandstone, about 6,906 m2, with roughly 15,000 oak barrels. The producer's own site says about 12,900.
Wines age long in barrel and are racked by hand twice a year, fined with egg whites and bottled unfiltered, then rest in bottle before release.
The cellar is open to professionals only, by appointment.
Taste dots: very dry (producer); medium body; fresh acidity (6.5 g/l); fine, dusty tannins.
Flavor icons from the notes: wild strawberry, tobacco, leather, forest floor.
Window 2020 to 2028: Atkin 2020 to 2028, Wine Advocate 2021 to 2028.
Decant an hour: no source gives advice.
Roast lamb and aged cheese added to the producer's roast meats and game.

conflicts: Production: producer sheet 80,000 bottles; merchant citing a critic 75,000.
Graciano: Decanter 3%; producer says only 'the rest' for Mazuelo and Graciano; Enbotella shows percentages that sum to 105%.
Tondonia planting: 1913 to 1914 (producer) vs 1914 (Haro tourism) vs replanting 1901 to 1907 (Decanter snippet).
Cellar barrels: about 12,900 (producer home page) vs about 15,000 (Haro tourism).
Window: Decanter 2021 to 2024, Atkin and Wine Advocate to 2028, CellarTracker 2020 to 2027.
Bosconia altitude: 465 m headline vs a 460 to 487 m range on the same page.
gaps: Exact release date: not found. Bottling Nov 2017 only.
Decanting advice: none found from producer or importer.
New oak share: not applicable or not stated; barrels described as used.
Native yeast, stems: not stated for this wine.
